newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba to use new technology for 64-MB DRAM - paper.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba to use new technology for 64-MB DRAM - paper.

text.p: Toshiba Corp will cut the cost of making 64-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips by using new technology developed for next-generation 256-bit chips, a Japanese daily said on Thursday.
The company will start using the new technology, with which it can reduce the size of a microchip, in the second half of 1997, about 18 months earlier than planned, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.

Using the new 0.25 micron technology, Toshiba can make more chips from one wafer than it can with the current 0.35 micron technology, the paper said. Toshiba officials were not immediately available for comment.
